```{r} #| label: setup #| message: false #| warning: false #| include: false library(tidyverse) library(scales) library(knitr) library(kableExtra) # fonts ---- library(extrafont) library(sysfonts) source("_common.R") # use font showtext::showtext_auto() # set theme ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_pogs( base_size = 15)) ``` ```{r} #| label: status #| results: "asis" #| echo: false # status ---- # polishing, restructuring, drafting, complete status("complete") ``` :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}
::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a categorical variable** ::: ```{r} #| label: full_code_display #| fig-asp: 1 #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '60%' #| out-width: '60%' #| fig-align: right library(ggwaffle) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) set.seed(1993) pog_collection <- tibble( pog_id = 1:100, type = sample(c("Milk caps", "Printed pogs", "Holographic", "Slammers"), size = 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.45, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10))) waffle_pogs <- ggwaffle::waffle_iron(pog_collection, aes_d(group = type), rows = 10) labs_waffle <- labs( title = "A Pogs collection (simulated)", subtitle = "100 pieces, one square each", x = "", y = "", fill = NULL) ggp2_waffle <- ggplot(data = waffle_pogs, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = group)) + ggwaffle::geom_waffle() + coord_equal() ggp2_waffle + labs_waffle + theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top") ``` :::: ## Description Waffle charts use small squares or icons to show how a whole thing is divided into parts, grouped into categories that fill a grid. They're useful for visualizing percentages or proportions from a total and can include a legend or labels to explain each category. Waffle chart legends should be positioned on top or bottom and justified horizontally to preserve shape and improve readability. We’ll build a waffle chart using the [`ggwaffle` package.](https://liamgilbey.github.io/ggwaffle/) ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Install packages. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: pkg_code_waffle #| code-fold: show #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| results: hide # ggwaffle is GitHub-only install.packages("pak") pak::pak("liamgilbey/ggwaffle") library(ggwaffle) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: In the mid 90s, kids traded and battled with Pogs: cardboard milk caps, printed and holographic pogs, and heavy plastic "slammers" used to flip them. We'll simulate a collection of 100 pieces with `sample()`, giving each type its own chance of turning up. Waffle charts require a special data transformation with `ggwaffle::waffle_iron()`. Set the `group` argument in `ggwaffle::aes_d()` to the categorical variable you want to see the relative counts for, and set `rows = 10` so 100 pieces fill a 10 by 10 grid. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same collection every time you run the code below. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: data_code_waffle #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true set.seed(1993) pog_collection <- tibble( pog_id = 1:100, type = sample(c("Milk caps", "Printed pogs", "Holographic", "Slammers"), size = 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.45, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10))) waffle_pogs <- ggwaffle::waffle_iron(pog_collection, aes_d(group = type), rows = 10) glimpse(waffle_pogs) ``` ::: ## Distribution A waffle chart is built for one special total: 100. When there are 100 squares, every square is one percent, so you can read a percentage just by counting squares. Below we'll move from the collection, to a picture, to the formula. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with the first ten pieces in the collection. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: count_values_waffle #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true head(pog_collection$type, 10) ``` ::: Six of these ten are milk caps, three are printed pogs, and one is holographic. Counting all 100 pieces gives us counts that are also percentages. The `expected` column is what we'd get if the collection matched the probabilities in `sample()` exactly. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: count_summary_waffle #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true pog_collection |> count(type) |> mutate(expected = c(15, 45, 30, 10)) ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: A bar model shows the collection as one bar of 100 pieces split into four parts. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: draw_bar_model_waffle #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true #| fig-asp: 0.45 pog_collection |> count(type) |> ggplot(aes(x = n, y = "100 pieces", fill = type)) + geom_col() + geom_text(aes(label = n), color = c("white", "white", "white", "black"), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5)) + labs(x = "Number of pieces", y = NULL, fill = "Type") ``` ::: A waffle chart is the same bar folded into rows of 10. Each column of the waffle below is ten pieces, so the milk caps fill a little more than four columns and the slammers fill a little more than one. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: draw_waffle #| fig-asp: 1 #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true ggplot(data = waffle_pogs, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = group)) + ggwaffle::geom_waffle() + coord_equal() + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) + theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top") ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Every piece in the collection is an independent draw from four types, so the four counts follow a [multinomial distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinomial_distribution): $$ (N_{\text{milk}}, N_{\text{printed}}, N_{\text{holo}}, N_{\text{slam}}) \sim \text{Multinomial}(n = 100, \; p = (0.45, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10)) $$ With $n = 100$, the expected count for each type is its probability times 100, which is the same number as its percentage. The counts wobble around those expectations by about $\sqrt{100\,p\,(1 - p)}$ pieces: about 5 for milk caps and 3 for slammers. Our collection has `r sum(pog_collection$type == "Slammers")` slammers instead of the expected 10, a difference of a little more than one standard deviation. Change the number in `set.seed()` and the squares trade places, but they always add to 100. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"} - Create labels with `labs()` - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` - Map the `x` and `y` to the `x` and `y` axes - Map `group` to `fill` - Add `ggwaffle::geom_waffle()` - Keep the squares square with `coord_equal()` - Remove the axis text and grid lines, and move the legend to the top with `theme()` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: code_graph_waffle #| code-fold: show #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' labs_waffle <- labs( title = "A Pogs collection (simulated)", subtitle = "100 pieces, one square each", x = "", y = "", fill = NULL) ggp2_waffle <- ggplot(data = waffle_pogs, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = group)) + ggwaffle::geom_waffle() + coord_equal() ggp2_waffle + labs_waffle + theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top") ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ```{r} #| label: create_graph_waffle #| fig-asp: 1 #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 labs_waffle <- labs( title = "A Pogs collection (simulated)", subtitle = "100 pieces, one square each", x = "", y = "", fill = NULL) ggp2_waffle <- ggplot(data = waffle_pogs, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = group)) + ggwaffle::geom_waffle() + coord_equal() ggp2_waffle + labs_waffle + theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top") ```
